T: Old oaks, planted in rows once. The rows have wandered off over the centuries, the way rows do.
k: A clipped hedge, taller than you. On this side, at least, somebody still trims it.
^: An arch cut through the hedge: the way into the royal maze.
r: White roses, hundreds of them. Somebody has kept them alive for five hundred years.
u: A fountain of white stone, still running.
The water is so clear you can count the coins at the bottom. Nobody has taken one.

lines: A fountain of white stone, still running after five hundred years.
In the water stand the old king and his queen, hand in hand. He is laughing at something. She is looking down the path, as if she is waiting for someone.
The plaque reads: FOR OUR QUEEN, WHO PLANTED THIS FOREST. MAY IT OUTGROW US ALL.
(So why does it feel like you have?)
